Fontlex Relaxed Math

The box below is a plain text box holding math the way people type it in plain text: (a+b)/(c+d), x^2, sqrt(x). The font typesets it as you type: fractions, roots, accents, superscripts and subscripts, laid out by the text engine that lays out the letters. Ordinary text stays ordinary, so and/or, w/o, dates and paths are left alone. The characters stay exactly as typed. No script on this page lays anything out.

  • Try (a+b)/(c+d), x^2, or sqrt(x).
  • Copying preserves exactly what you typed.
  • Spaces inside formulas and mixed Greek/Latin text have limitations; see below.

What it typesets

  • Fractions: 1/2, x/2, 2a/3, (a+b)/(c+d), f(x)/2, 1/(1+1/x). Parentheses around a whole part go; with a script after them they stay: (a+b)^2/c.
  • Scripts: x^2, x^(n+1), x^-1, x_1, H_2O, and both at once, stacked: x_i^2.
  • Roots: sqrt(x^2+1).
  • Accents, over letters: hat(x), bar(z), vec(AB), dot(x), ddot(x), tilde(f).
  • Symbols: <= >= != -> => +- become ≤ ≥ ≠ → ⇒ ±. Greek letters and other symbols can be typed as themselves.

That is all: this isn't LaTeX or a general math engine. For a little LaTeX, see Fontlex Math, a subset as well.

What stays text

  • A fraction's parts are numbers (12, 3.5), a number and a letter (2a), one letter, a group in parentheses, a call like f(x) or sin(x), a root or an accent, each with its scripts. Longer words make no fraction: and/or, km/h, page/2.
  • Two lone letters make a fraction only in an expression (a+b/c, x = a/b), so w/o, n/a and I/O stay as they are.
  • Slashes in a row (a/b/c, 10/23/2026, //) make none, nor does any slash in a run of characters where one touches a longer word (tr/a-z/A-Z/).
  • An accent's parentheses hold letters and nothing else, so dot(a,b) and vec(x+1) stay text, and so do np.dot(x) and ahat(x), where the name follows a letter, digit, point or underscore.
  • No script touches another underscore, and a number has no subscript: file_1_2, 1_000 stay text.

Limits and ambiguous notation

  • Nesting. Constructs go inside constructs 3 deep, with at most 2 fractions inside one another, and at most 24 characters in a construct that isn't inside another. Past that, a construct stays as its characters.
  • Spaces. A space inside a construct leaves it as its characters: write (a+b)/2, not (a + b)/2. Spaces between formulas are fine.
  • Greek and Latin. Chrome and Firefox shape runs of Greek and Latin letters apart, and a construct can't span two runs, so there e^(iπ) stays as its characters. Safari lays it out.
  • Ambiguous notation. A part is a whole word, so 2/3x is 2 over 3x, and x^2y is x² followed by y. A number over a number is always a fraction, so 7/8 bit and a date like 6/14 are typeset too. On its own, a/b stays text, as w/o does.
  • Lines and the caret. Each line is read on its own. A construct that isn't complete yet stays as its characters until it is. Inside a fraction the caret stays at the fraction's start: its glyphs are drawn where they belong, but take no room of their own.
  • Where it's checked. HarfBuzz (the shaper in Chrome and Firefox) and Core Text (Safari, macOS) against a model of the notation. By screenshot, Chrome and Safari's WebKit on macOS, and Chromium and Firefox on Linux and Windows. Native Windows apps, which shape with DirectWrite, don't lay it out: DirectWrite ignores a kind of lookup the font relies on (details).

How it works

124 passes read each line the way the rules above say, and rewrite it as the LaTeX that lays out the same: (a+b)/(c+d) as \frac{a+b}{c+d}, with the parentheses as its braces and a \frac and braces that the line doesn't have inserted as glyphs that draw nothing. Then Fontlex Math's own passes lay it out. The font has 61,193 glyphs and 2,075 substitution and 301 positioning lookups.

Results

Each line is shaped with the font, what it draws is read back from the glyphs (characters by name and size, rules from their outlines), and compared with a separate Python model of the notation (relaxed.py), to the font unit.
